done_when: The customer is verified and logged, and the chosen savings account is open. The customer has been told its funding status, or the 30-day funding deadline and the opening deposit minimum. They have also been told any fee from being below the minimum balance and any feature notes that apply: the paperless requirement, Silver terms, the ATM rebate cap, what the documents say about paper statements, and how the card bonus applies. Alternatively, an eligibility check failed and the customer has been told what to resolve; for short tenure, the date they become eligible, checked fresh against records. Or the opening failed, and the customer has been told why and offered a transfer. Any requested checking opening or closure follows.

steps.do: Compare every personal savings account against the customer's needs and recommend ONE that meets them all. Apply card-holder benefits only when get_credit_cards shows the card. Exclude an account when its opening deposit or ongoing minimum is above the customer's maximum, its free withdrawals are below the customer's monthly count, it lacks ATM rebates the customer needs, or its APY is below their target. Silver Plus Account: 15 free withdrawals, 3.0% Tier 1 APY below $15,000, ATM rebates up to 25, savings goals tracking, $1,000 opening deposit, $2,500 minimum and an $8.00 fee below it. Withdrawals beyond 15 may incur an excess fee. Gold Account: standard $10,000 minimum ($5,000 with a Gold Rewards Card), 20 withdrawals, ATM rebates up to $30. If two accounts fit equally, or no single account meets every need, explain the trade-off and ask the customer which matters most.
